text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press at the weekend. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- European Investment Bank gave a 70 million ECU ($87.5 million) 20-year loan for building and upgrading roads in the central Transylvania region.
- The price of gold on Bucharest markets rose by some 10 percent soon after the increase in leu-dollar exchange rate.
- Amoco Corp. will continue its activity in Romania in areas other than retail petrol trade.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania signed an accord with Russia to boost its import capacity for natural gas from current levels of seven billion to 10.5 billion by the year 2000 14 billion by the year 2005.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- A quarter of Romanian girls aged between six and nine are illiterate according to a U.N. survey.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Belgium is expected to pass a bill to allow NATO Partnership for Peace countries like Romania to accredit a residence mission at NATO headquarters in Brussels.
ADEVARUL
- Romania's 16 presidential candidates are to attend a live television debate on October 31, at 1900 local/1700 GMT on the state television's channel one.

- Two journalists from daily Ziua were sentenced to one year in jail and more for "defaming the state authority", after a series of articles alleging that President Ion Iliescu was a former Soviet KGB spy.

- Former spy Constantin Bucur -- who accused the Romanian Intelligence Service of phonetapping -- is prosecuted for transmitting and disclosing classified information. If convicted, he faces a sentence of up to seven years in jail.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Half the population in Garliciu village near the Black Sea port of Constanta are HIV-infected due to many of its women acting as prostitutes in the port, medical authorities said.
ZIUA
- Some 82 percent of Romania's voters said they were determined to cast votes in November 3 elections, a poll commissioned by private PROTV television to IMAS showed.
- The poll shows the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) 1.5 percentage points ahead of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
- President Ion Iliescu is far out in front in the poll for the presidential election, with 36.5 percent, ahead of CDR candidate Emil Constantinescu, credited with 24.7 percent.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
